name: Box64: emulating the guest's MAP_32BIT requires a free HOST block below 2^31, found by find31bitBlockNearHint
required_postconditions: returned_address + size < 0x80000000 whenever the guest passed MAP_32BIT
Box64 strips MAP_32BIT from the host flags and substitutes its own search, because the host may not be x86-64 and MAP_32BIT only exists there
if the first attempt still lands above 0xffffffff Box64 unmaps it, reloads /proc/self/maps and retries once with MAP_FIXED into a block it believes free

failure_sink.description: if find31bitBlockNearHint returns nothing usable, MAP_FIXED is not added and the plain mmap result is returned to the guest as-is. A guest that asked for MAP_32BIT can therefore receive a high address with no error; the truncation happens in the guest, not in Box64.

source_locations.symbol: if((flags&MAP_32BIT) && !(flags&MAP_FIXED)) { // MAP_32BIT only exist on x86_64!
addr = find31bitBlockNearHint(old_addr, length, 0) - the function name states the 2^31 bound

extraction_limitations: the '< 2^31' requirement is stated only by the helper's name and by Linux's MAP_32BIT semantics; the post-check at line 3300 tests against 0xffffffff, so the source is internally inconsistent about which bound it enforces. Neither bound is expressible in this schema.
size 4096 is representative; the requirement is independent of size.
find31bitBlockNearHint is not in the file excerpt read; its bound was not verified by reading its body.

x_campaign.rationale: Nothing in the expressible part of this request can fail on x86-64 Linux - it is a 4 KiB anonymous RW mapping with no address. I expect the tool to miss the below-2GiB constraint entirely, which is the point of including it.
x_campaign.note_after_schema_fix: address_max replaced the identity flag, which was only ever a stand-in for a range bound and made the analyzer report a contradiction it had manufactured.
